full_judgment:
3. The defendant opposite parties No. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending, inter alia. that the plaintiff and his two brothers purchased the land sold by 3 kabalas and that the vendees executed and registered 3 deeds of agreement of reconveyance for period of 12 years and that the Miscellaneous cases for redemption were correctly filed and legally allowed by the Magistrate and the possession of the suit land was restored to Nazar Ali on 30-4-74 and that after the death of Nazar Ali his heirs sold the entire land on 4-5-76 to the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 and delivered possession of the suit land. 

 5. Md. Shamsul Hoque, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that in view of the fact that the plaintiff has filed the suit for declaration of title and that the defendant opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 have fraudulently entered into an agreement of reconveyance and of declaration that the disputed order passed by the Magistrate 1st Class in respect of the suit land under President's Order No. 88 of 1972 is illegal, void as the plaintiff is not a signatory to the alleged deed of reconveyance and that the alleged executants the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 had no interest in the suit and the court of appeal below erred in law in not holding that the transaction is an out and out sale inasmuch as, even if the same is a complete usufructuary mortgage section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act will have no application to the transaction which was past and closed. 

 7. Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act reads as under: 

 "95A. Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force any transfer of holding or of potion or share thereof either by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey or where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess, and to enjoy the usufruct of such holding or portion or share thereof for a specified period in lieu of such consideration, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a completed usufructuary mortgage for period not exceeding seven years and the provisions of section 95 shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Second Amendment) Order, 1972 (PW No. 88 of 1972) 

 8. Section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is also read as follows: 

 9. In this case the transfer of the land was made by way of out and out sale dated 6-5-60 standing in the name of the plaintiff and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 but the agreement to reconvey the land was registered only by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. Thus it shows that though the transaction appears to be one under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act being a complete usufructuary mortgage for being accompanied by a contemporaneous agreement for reconveyance but the plaintiff in whose name the deed stands is not signatory to the agreement of reconveyance. Even if the transaction is deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years but it was stipulated in the said agreement covering the period for 12 years from 6-5-60 and 30-6-60 for reconveyance of the land in question. 

 10. Under the law then prevalent on 6-5-60 and 30-6-60 the transaction could not be deemed to be a mortgage in view of the proviso to clause (c) of section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act but section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as amended by President's Order No. 137 of 1972 which came into fore on 4-11-72 incorporated the word "whether before or after the 28th June, 1972 any transaction must be deemed to be complete usufructuary mortgage" but out Appellate Division in the case of Abdul Mannan & Ors vs. Kulada Ranjan Mowali & Ors. reported in 31 DLR (AD) 195 has held that the use of the word Malek in place of the word raiyat or tenant for giving retrospective effect to section 87 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act could not go back to any date before the provision of Part V had come into force. 

 12. Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into effect from 3-8-72. If we calculate 2 years had expired on 5-5-72 and 29-5-72 and thus the transaction seems to be not alive on the date of coming into operation of President's Order No. 88 of 1972 on 3-8-72 and, as such, the transaction is past and closed. This finds support in the case of Bangladesh vs. Haji Abdul Ganir eported in 32 DLR (AD) 233. In a recent decision in the case of Abdul Khaleque Sarnamat vs. Abdul Khaleque Sarnamat and another reported in 1 BLC (AD) 90 it has been held that "in the instant case the parties agreed by the transaction in question that the period of mortgage will be for 4 years beginning from 24-6-67. So, the transaction cannot be said to be alive and subsisting on the date of promulgation of President's Order No. 88 of 72 i.e. on 3-8-72. It was a transaction past and closed". 

 13. Apart from the provision of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the remedies under section 95 of the said Act, the remedy of civil Court is always available to the mortgagor in case of a mortgage, the limitation of which for redemption is within a period of 60 years from the date of accrual of his right of redemption and a suit can be filed for redemption of the mortgage as has been held in the case of Abu Bakkar vs. Nazir Ahmed 34 DLR (AD) 237. Although a mortgagor can redeem a complete usufructuary mortgage either under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act or by way of a suit within 60 years from the date of accrual of his right for redemption but in the instant facts and circumstances of the case the transaction cannot be said to be alive and subsisting on the date of promulgation of President's Order No. 88 of 72 and the transaction was accordingly past and closed. The defendants though alleged that they are entitled to benefit of 12 months as provided under the Bangladesh (Legal Proceedings) Order, 1972 (President' Order No. 12 of 1972) but the said order has no manner of application in case of public document as has been held in 1 BLC (AD) 90 and moreso in respect of any public document also when the period of limitation did not expire between the period from 1st March, 1971 to 1st March 1972. Another striking feature of the present case is that the plaintiff has been able to prove that he purchased the suit land by his own money and for his own benefit by Kabala dated 6-5-60 and 30-6-60 through defendant Nos. 1 and 2 but the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 have fraudulently inserted their names in the kabalas and also fraudulently executed the deed of reconveyance by themselves. The plaintiff having been able to prove that the plaintiff has the alleged title, interest and possession in the suit land, the alleged deed of agreement executed by defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in favour of the vendor is of no legal consequence and moreso it could not effect the right, title, interest and possession in the suit land of plaintiff and in that view of the matter the plaintiff alone having right, title and interest in the suit land on the basis of kabalas dated 6-5-60 and 30-6-60 the alleged deed of reconveyance executed by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 who have no interest in the suit land and have fraudulently inserted their names in the kabalas could not bind the plaintiff so as to treat the transaction to be a complete usufructuary mortgage as contemplated under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 14. The trial Court on consideration of the materials on record has found the transaction to be an out and out sale and same is past and closed having 12 years been expired prior to coming into operation of President's Order No. 88 of 1972 incorporating section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and that the plaintiff has right, title and interest in the suit land and paid consideration for the kabalas and thus acquired good title over the suit land.
